video_title: How to Get Rich in Crypto in the Next 3 Years w/ Kyle Soska
gist: Rayo Capital CIO Kyle Soska explains the Hyperliquid perp thesis and TGE-night trade, why he thinks cycle lows are in and a market maturing toward being right equals making money, the Bitcoin quantum overhang, and trading psychology lessons including the EigenLayer ETH exit and the missed TRB trade.

themes.theme: Crypto cycle regime and market maturity

insights.claim: Soska believes crypto has inflected and that cycle lows are probably in for majors like Bitcoin and ETH, calling it a very durable bottom.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Supports a constructive stance on majors after a long bear phase.
insights.quote: I think cycle lows are probably in.

insights.claim: Crypto has run out of new participants: Binance had about 250 million KYC users after 2021 and the industry approached 6-7% of global population, which he estimates is 30-40% saturation of everyone who will ever trade crypto, so next-cycle buyers are not first-timers.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: A saturated, more experienced base implies less naive-retail-driven blow-off behavior and a re-rating of quality over junk.
insights.quote: we're at like 30 or 40% saturation of every eligible person who will ever participate in crypto

insights.claim: Because nobody is new anymore, he argues from 2026 onward being right will also make money, reversing 2017-2025 when being right and making money diverged; assets with durable cash-flow or permanent-role narratives are outperforming while bad assets underperform.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Favor fundamentally-narrated assets and concentrated holds over churning low-quality tokens.
insights.quote: being right and making money start looking a lot like the same thing

insights.claim: Meme coins are a gambling tool that do not fit the maturing market, and he is not enthusiastic about Pump or FOMO-type trenches, although he doubts there remain many uninitiated tribes with money to burn.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Fade the thesis that retail onboarding via meme apps drives the next leg; look at higher-quality assets.

insights.claim: Hold times collapsed to minutes in the trenches, but the right approach is the opposite: someone holding a high-conviction bag for six months to two years outperforms people who change their view daily.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Outsized returns come from holding out-of-consensus positions through the slow process of consensus forming.

insights.claim: Big winning trades must take months or years because it is extremely unlikely that something nobody sees is seen by everybody within a week; markets pay when an out-of-consensus idea becomes consensus.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Size and hold for the duration of the consensus-formation process rather than trading around.

insights.claim: Soska no longer believes in the four-year cycle but respects it because others do; smart money learns and front-runs the pattern, so cycles may shorten to roughly 3.5 years then 3, then lengthen.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Cycle-timing strategies get arbitraged away; expect distorted timing around the supposed anniversary bottom.
insights.quote: I no longer believe in the four-ear cycle

insights.claim: Current vibes are good but mostly from crypto-native capital that swung from not thinking about crypto to max allocated in three months; there is little tourist capital and nobody out of crypto for five years has re-entered with size.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Sentiment is crowded in natives and the next marginal buyer has not arrived, so upside from outside inflows is still ahead.

insights.claim: In summer, memory stocks like Micron moved 10% a day while Bitcoin just did not move, drawing prominent long-time crypto personalities away to trade memory stocks and AI names before they returned to crypto.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Crypto competes for trader attention with volatile AI/memory equities, and attention returns as crypto moves.

insights.claim: Narrative and vibes now matter more than cash-flow fundamentals across all markets, and even Tesla's multiple is largely memetic, so a deteriorating vibe can take a stock from 40x to 20x or 10x.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Track narrative sentiment as a primary valuation driver for crypto and equities.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid and the perpetual futures thesis

insights.claim: Soska and Flood held a multi-year thesis that perpetual futures are the key instrument, rooted in his BitMEX research, and moved their trading to Hyperliquid in 2023 after seeing how many small details the team got right; Hyperliquid became their highest-conviction position.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Backing the product you personally use and the team that is visibly competent was the path to their biggest trade.

insights.claim: On TGE night Flood swept all the cash into HYPE while Soska slept, buying on pure gut after prior preparation including top three or four per token holder rank, Silicon Terminal integration and a generous airdrop; the price then rose every day for about 30 days.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Prepared conviction plus a willingness to size aggressively on the day is what converted a good trade into a generational one.

insights.claim: Soska argues Hyperliquid has won the onchain perp game and is roughly at the limit of what a decentralized perp venue can feasibly achieve; he sees the competitors like Lighter as rinse-and-repeat third, fourth or fifth versions.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Avoid second-tier perp DEX clones; own the winner.
insights.quote: Hyperlid, which I think has won the onchain game

insights.claim: The perp market has tiers: Hyperliquid at the onchain limit, Binance as the best centralized implementation, and a possible future deterministic-latency FPGA centralized perp exchange from someone like CME or the rumored Citadel/BlackRock/Texas exchange; Soska is uninterested in the gray area between Hyperliquid and that endgame.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: A tradfi-grade centralized perp venue is the main long-run competitive threat, and mid-tier perp DEXs are squeezed.

insights.claim: Binance has about 50 million KYC perp traders and its perp-to-options volume ratio is roughly 12 to 1 (transcript garbled); this long-running experiment suggests that given a choice, users pick perps, so converting zero-day options traders in US brokerages to perps could be massive even at 10% conversion.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: The Hyperliquid bull case beyond crypto rests on taking share from the tradfi options market and on US regulatory access.
insights.quote: if you gave them a fair shot at trying Hyperlquid or you know any other purpose product

insights.claim: He says a HYPE move to 200-300 requires either a wild bull market where everyone is flush or genuine share capture from TradFi options; with HYPE around 94-95 at recording, he thinks the market has largely come around to seeing Hyperliquid's quality, and major wallets like Trust Wallet, Phantom and MetaMask are integrating.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: The remaining upside depends on non-consensus beliefs about US regulation and tier-one distribution.

insights.claim: Soska predicts HYPE will break 100 because round numbers act as magnetic orbits, citing silver nearing 97 and Bitcoin breaking 100K after 96K; he jokes about a hundy roll.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Light-hearted, but flags 100 as a key psychological level for HYPE.
insights.quote: the honey roll is is is pre-ordained

insights.claim: Soska and Flood trade around HYPE; during the USDH ticker auction when Paxos, Athena and PayPal all praised Hyperliquid, Soska read the unanimous niceness as a possible local top and wanted to sell.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Extreme consensus praise from counterparties can mark short-term euphoria.

insights.claim: Soska says regulation excuses are mostly cope: if a product has real product-market fit the public will pressure lawmakers to legalize it, as with Uber, and Bitcoin and Hyperliquid never asked for intervention.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of projects whose bull case depends on a regulatory unlock or a fee switch.
insights.quote: If the world isn't screaming to make your product legal, it's just not that good

insights.claim: Soska thinks Bitcoin's price would be about double without the quantum overhang, because large holders, with Galaxy facilitating sales for clients holding about 80,000 BTC, will not accept even a 1% chance of catastrophe in five years, and wealth managers cannot allocate while quantum firms say they may crack Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Quantum uncertainty is a structural cap on institutional and whale demand independent of imminence.
insights.quote: the price is probably half of what it would be

insights.claim: Quantum computing firms have an incentive to exaggerate cracking ECDSA to raise money, similar to AI doomerism from Anthropic and OpenAI, which hurts Bitcoin's vibes even if the threat is not imminent.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Fundraising incentives on the quantum side feed the overhang; treat headlines accordingly.

insights.claim: A quantum upgrade is technically known and possible today and many recent transaction formats are accidentally quantum safe because hash-based, but bigger signatures would slow an already slow chain, and almost every small quantum-safe signature candidate was broken in the last four or five months.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Technical progress toward a solution is slower than hoped, so resolution timing is uncertain.

insights.claim: He expects a contentious fight like the 2017-2018 block wars over a Bitcoin quantum fix, so the sidelined money will not return until one proposal gains quorum, after which Bitcoin should reprice materially higher as cashed-out capital from the last year or so front-runs the upgrade.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: The catalyst to watch is a champion proposal, testnet and visible quorum; Bitcoin trades fine meanwhile on debasement and US fiscal concerns.

insights.claim: Zcash governance is smooth, with token holder votes passing quickly such as cutting block time to about 25 seconds, while Bitcoin forks like the anti-ordinals spam attempt took a year and a half and left community leaders not speaking; this makes Zcash better positioned for post-quantum upgrades, though throughput is currently very low.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Governance speed is a differentiator for Zcash's long-term case as larger post-quantum signatures strain scalability.

insights.claim: Soska criticizes the Zcash bull case framed as insurance against Bitcoin, saying a token whose bull case names another token is a win for the other and one should like Zcash on its own merits.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Relative-framing narratives are weaker than standalone ones.

themes.theme: Ethereum, L1 tokens and the cycle-skip debate

insights.claim: Soska sold all ETH exposure within 48 hours near roughly $3,800 after hearing an EigenLayer foundation staffer on a Twitter Space admit she did not know where yield would come from to pay for about $11 billion of restaked TVL, as the original rent-economic-security model had no real buyers.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Candid comments from lower-level insiders in Twitter Spaces can be an early signal that an overvalued narrative is cracking.
insights.quote: I don't know where the yield is going to come from to pay these guys

insights.claim: He views both ETH and SOL as having failed as money while being priced as money, which made them good shorts, and says he is not a fan of L1 tokens in general, though if forced to choose he prefers Ethereum as the more pristine chain.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Low conviction in absolute L1 returns; any ETH exposure is relative.
insights.quote: I think both ETH and Soul failed as money

insights.claim: Soska floated CryptoPunks as potentially the best way to play ETH beta, arguing iconic distasteful early-NFT status gives value that other NFTs lack, and would mix ETH and Punks if long ETH.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: An idiosyncratic ETH-beta expression, not a high-conviction call.

insights.claim: He expects onchain trading to shift increasingly to stablecoin pairs rather than ETH or SOL pairs, weakening the use of L1 tokens as the money of their ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Undermines the monetary-premium argument for L1 tokens.

insights.claim: Cycle-skip theory, where last cycle's main character underperforms next cycle, resonates with Soska on a relative-strength basis for ETH over SOL, but he is not convinced ETH will do well in absolute terms.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Relative-strength framing only; no strong ETH accumulation planned.

insights.claim: Host Taiki's framework is that the best trade is a challenged top-five asset and a competitor taking share (Bitcoin Cash, ETH, SOL previously), with this cycle being HYPE relative to BNB and Zcash relative to Bitcoin; Soska called it quite sensible and said you can keep it simple.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: A simple challenger-versus-incumbent pairing approach Soska endorsed.

insights.claim: Soska says knowing too much hurts conviction: his early dismissal of DAO governance made 2021 hard and the left-curve/right-curve pattern means crypto rewards belief first and selling discipline later; the lesson is to stay about three months ahead of the crowd, not three years.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Being correct but too early is the same as being wrong in market terms.
insights.quote: I should have leaned in more towards entertaining the idea

insights.claim: The TRB episode in 2023: a $25M market cap coin with 80% of spot supply cornered, held at Bit Forex, negative funding, and a New Year's Day run from about $120 to $600 then a one-candle crash; Soska understood it but did not trade it out of fear of losing, and calls it his main weakness lesson.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Cornered low-float perps can be predictably pumped; the cost of excess risk aversion is missing understood trades.
insights.quote: this should have been like one of the trades

insights.claim: He attributes the TRB manipulation to whoever ran Bit Forex, which exit-scammed two months later, but thinks it was likely not done with Binance's permission and that Binance screens such coins because it is toxic for their business.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Tier-2 exchange custody of cornered supply is a red flag for squeeze setups on majors' perp listings.

insights.claim: Shorting requires acute knowledge of supply dynamics; Grass token shorts got squeezed because float was far tighter than assumed, so speculative shorts are best done in diversified baskets of 10-15 coins while hedging holdings and unlocks is the responsible use.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Short baskets and only where float is understood; avoid single low-float names.
insights.quote: I think it's important to only short things you understand

insights.claim: Soska handles tilt by sizing down to test size, about 5% of his portfolio, rather than taking breaks, and scales back up when he is in rhythm with the market; he finds traders go on streaks.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Position sizing as the mechanism for emotional regulation.

insights.claim: Making trades inconvenient, for example stepping away from the screen or walking without headphones, raises the threshold for entering trades and filters out noise trades.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Reducing friction to trade leads to overtrading.

insights.claim: Rayo is all proprietary capital, and Soska says owning the downside makes them less levered than peers because outside managers with capped downside swing for the fences.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Incentive structure explains manager risk-taking differences.

insights.claim: Soska and Flood complement each other: Flood is the gifted high-conviction buyer, while Soska is the cynical seller who looks for reasons to sell, such as the EigenLayer and USDH episodes.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Pairing a buyer and a skeptic works well as a team structure.

insights.claim: For small portfolios, Soska advises keeping a day job and participating part-time; at $1M-$10M, hit many singles, wait years for a BitMEX/ChatGPT-style moment and size into it, and never blow up or tilt.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Patience and survival matter more than forcing 10x trades.

insights.claim: Soska's 2017 spot trading: a $100,000 book doing about $70-80 million monthly volume on Kraken, with the easy-money environment where up 5% on the day meant you held the worst coin; he notes drawdown psychology has flipped from thanks for cheaper prices in 2018-2021 to damn it, I'm max allocated now.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Market psychology in drawdowns is now sell-first, so sharp declines may run faster with thinner dip-buying.

themes.theme: Crypto's real products and what is coming onchain

insights.claim: His long-held view is that crypto's lasting contributions are 24/7 trading, stablecoins and perpetual futures, which he expects to be ubiquitous in TradFi within about five years, and crypto founders are increasingly calling themselves finance.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Crypto is a sandbox whose winning products migrate into mainstream finance, favoring owners of those rails.

insights.claim: Tokenized equities are coming onchain: everyone at the conference had a tokenization plan, and while there won't be ten winners, higher quality assets onchain would allow building stable appreciating portfolios.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: The next onchain wave is quality assets rather than meme coins.

insights.claim: Soska invests mostly in products he personally uses, saying the investments he hates are those where he does not like the product but bets someone else will.
insights.speaker: Kyle Soska
insights.so_what: Product-usage conviction makes it easier to see when a thesis breaks.
